title: Seventh Word Proof For Patience And Reliance Weakness As A Document

questions.question: What are the two medicines named at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: One is trust in Allah together with patience, and the other is depending on the Creator’s power while being confident in His wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, why does a person who depends on Allah have less reason to be overwhelmed by fear?
questions.answer: Because he knows he is relying on the Lord of all things, whose command is irresistible and whose care is greater than any disaster.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the response of a believer when hardship strikes?
questions.answer: He turns back to Allah, remembers that he belongs to Him, and places his trust in his merciful Lord.

questions.question: What surprising idea does the passage present about weakness and fear of Allah?
questions.answer: It says they can bring a kind of sweetness and peace when they lead a person to seek refuge in Allah.

questions.question: What example is used to explain how helplessness can feel safe rather than humiliating?
questions.answer: The example is of a very young child who feels secure by recognizing his need and finding safety with his mother.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this example is still limited?
questions.answer: Because even a mother’s mercy is only a tiny sign of Allah’s much greater mercy.

questions.question: How do the wise deal with fear of Allah according to the passage?
questions.answer: They treat it as something that drives them toward Allah’s protection, not something that pushes them away.

questions.question: What does it mean that they declare themselves free of strength and power?
questions.answer: It means they do not rely on themselves as if they were self-sufficient, but admit their need for Allah.

questions.question: In this passage, what role do powerlessness and fear play for a believer?
questions.answer: They become means of seeking Allah’s help and mercy.

questions.question: What is one central message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Real safety and inner peace come from recognizing human weakness and relying fully on Allah’s power, wisdom, and mercy.

questions.question: Which two spiritual remedies are introduced in the passage?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah with patience, and relying on the Creator’s power while trusting His wisdom.

questions.question: What question does the passage raise right after naming these remedies?
questions.answer: It asks whether these remedies truly work in the way being claimed.

questions.question: How is that question answered?
questions.answer: It is answered strongly and directly by saying that they truly do work.

questions.question: What description of Allah’s power supports this answer?
questions.answer: Allah is described as the sovereign of the world whose command brings things into existence immediately.

questions.question: How is human weakness presented in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Human weakness becomes a reason to lean on Allah rather than a reason to lose hope.

questions.question: When facing a severe trial, what attitude should a believer take according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should remember that he belongs to Allah and return to Him, then place his trust in Allah.

questions.question: What unusual claim is made about fear of Allah?
questions.answer: The passage says that fearing Allah can contain a deep kind of comfort and joy.

questions.question: How does the example of the baby help explain this claim?
questions.answer: It shows that someone who knows his helplessness may find safety by turning to the one who lovingly protects him.

questions.question: What does the comparison teach about the relationship between divine mercy and human mercy?
questions.answer: Human mercy is small and limited, while divine mercy is far greater and is the true source behind all mercy.

questions.question: Why have the wise openly admitted their weakness?
questions.answer: Because they saw that honesty about their weakness leads them to rely on Allah instead of themselves.

questions.question: According to the final sentence of the passage, what have they made into a means of drawing near to Allah?
questions.answer: They have made their helplessness and their fear of Allah into a way of seeking His acceptance and protection.

questions.question: What is the first medicine mentioned in the passage, and what two qualities are joined with it?
questions.answer: The first medicine is trusting Allah, joined with patience and confidence in the Creator’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: What view of Allah makes trust reasonable in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah is presented as the ruler over everything, with complete authority and ability.

questions.question: How does the passage connect belief in Allah’s control with courage in hardship?
questions.answer: It teaches that a person who knows Allah is in control does not need to collapse in fear before disasters.

questions.question: What words of remembrance are given as an example for someone in calamity?
questions.answer: The believer remembers that he belongs to Allah and that his return is to Him.

questions.question: Why is this remembrance important in the logic of the passage?
questions.answer: It helps the person accept hardship with faith and direct his heart back to Allah.

questions.question: What kind of person is said to find delight even in weakness?
questions.answer: A person who truly knows Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage praise fear in general, or a specific kind of fear? Explain.
questions.answer: It praises fear of Allah, because that fear leads a person to refuge, humility, and nearness to Him.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the image of a child with his mother?
questions.answer: Feeling small and dependent can be comforting when one turns to a source of love and protection.

questions.question: Why does the passage bring up a mother’s compassion?
questions.answer: To give a human example of caring protection that readers can easily understand.

questions.question: What correction does the passage immediately make after that example?
questions.answer: It says a mother’s compassion is only a tiny reflection of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What have the wise rejected about themselves?
questions.answer: They have rejected the idea that they possess real independent strength and power.

questions.question: Summarize the passage’s teaching in one sentence.
questions.answer: A believer gains peace by admitting his weakness, fearing Allah properly, and seeking shelter in Allah’s unlimited mercy and power.

questions.question: According to the passage, what two remedies heal the human condition being discussed?
questions.answer: Reliance on Allah with patience, and trust in the Creator’s power and wise decree.

questions.question: What kind of person is described as having little to fear?
questions.answer: A person who knows his own helplessness and places himself under Allah’s care.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s command mentioned in the discussion of fear?
questions.answer: To show that the One being relied on has complete power over all things.

questions.question: In a crisis, what does the believer do first inwardly?
questions.answer: He remembers his belonging to Allah and his return to Him.

questions.question: What does this inward response lead him to do?
questions.answer: It leads him to put his trust in his compassionate Lord.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge normal human thinking about weakness?
questions.answer: It says weakness is not only painful; when connected to faith, it can become a source of comfort.

questions.question: What emotional idea is attached to fear of Allah in the passage?
questions.answer: Fear of Allah is linked with sweetness, safety, and refuge.

questions.question: How does the child illustration support that emotional idea?
questions.answer: The child’s awareness of need makes him run toward loving protection, not away from it.

questions.question: What is the purpose of saying that all mothers’ mercy is only a brief reflection?
questions.answer: The purpose is to direct the reader from familiar human kindness to the far greater mercy of Allah.

questions.question: What behavior of the wise is praised near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: They openly acknowledge their weakness and seek protection in Allah instead of trusting themselves.

questions.question: What does it mean that they use weakness and fear as an intercessor?
questions.answer: It means they let those feelings move them to sincere humility and supplication before Allah.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage’s tone?
questions.answer: It is encouraging and faith-building, teaching that dependence on Allah is a strength, not a defeat.

questions.question: Name the two medicines explained in this passage.
questions.answer: They are trust in Allah with patience, and reliance on the Creator’s power together with confidence in His wisdom.

questions.question: What argument does the passage make for why these medicines are effective?
questions.answer: It argues that when a person relies on Allah, he is relying on the One who has full control and unmatched power.

questions.question: How is human helplessness described indirectly in the passage?
questions.answer: It is treated like proof that a person needs Allah and should not rely on himself.

questions.question: What should a believer remember during a major loss or calamity?
questions.answer: He should remember that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: What spiritual result comes from remembering that?
questions.answer: It helps him trust Allah instead of giving in to panic or hopelessness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can someone who knows Allah experience even in weakness?
questions.answer: He can experience peace and even a kind of joy.

questions.question: Why is the example of a baby fitting for this teaching?
questions.answer: Because a baby naturally survives by recognizing need and finding safety in caring protection.

questions.question: In the example, what makes the child’s helplessness something sweet rather than bitter?
questions.answer: His helplessness leads him to the security of loving care.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the mercy of mothers compared with Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: A mother’s mercy is real but very small compared with Allah’s vast mercy.

questions.question: What attitude toward personal strength do the wise adopt?
questions.answer: They stop trusting in their own power and admit their complete need for Allah.

questions.question: What do they do after admitting that need?
questions.answer: They seek refuge in Allah through their weakness and fear of Him.

questions.question: What are the two medicines, and what spiritual problem are they meant to answer?
questions.answer: They are trust in Allah with patience, and reliance on the Creator’s power and wisdom; they answer the problem of human weakness and fear in hardship.

questions.question: How does the passage use Allah’s absolute power to strengthen the believer’s heart?
questions.answer: It reminds the believer that the One he depends on can bring about whatever He wills without difficulty.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about fear when a person truly trusts Allah?
questions.answer: Fear loses its control over him because he knows he is under Allah’s care.

questions.question: What statement of faith is given as a model response to calamity?
questions.answer: The believer affirms that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: Why is this response more than just words in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it expresses surrender, trust, and acceptance of Allah’s rule.

questions.question: What kind of pleasure is described in connection with impotence and fear of Allah?
questions.answer: It is the pleasure of finding refuge, safety, and closeness to Allah.

questions.question: What human relationship is used to help explain this spiritual idea?
questions.answer: The relationship between a small child and his mother.

questions.question: What part of that relationship is most important for the comparison?
questions.answer: The child’s sense of need and his turning toward caring protection.

questions.question: How does the passage prevent readers from stopping at the human example?
questions.answer: It immediately teaches that human compassion is only a faint sign of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Who are the people described as understanding this truth well?
questions.answer: The wise are the ones described as understanding it.

questions.question: What have the wise chosen to do with their weakness and fear of Allah?
questions.answer: They have turned them into means of seeking Allah’s help and mercy.

questions.question: If you had to express the main point of the passage in everyday language, what would it be?
questions.answer: Don’t trust your own limited strength; admit your need, be patient, and lean on Allah, because that is where real peace is found.
